test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-II Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2025)
subject: general
question:
Water flows through a cylindrical pipe of internal diameter 21 cm at the rate of 8 m/s. What time, in minutes, would the pipe take to fill an empty rectangular tank of dimensions {12 m × 9 m times 4.41 m}?

(Rounded up to one decimal place) (Use pi=frac{22}7)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time to fill tank = Volume of Tank ÷ Volume Flow Rate per minute

Time = (L × B × H) ÷ (π × r² × v × 60)

Time = (12 × 9 × 4.41) ÷ [ (22/7) × (0.105)² × 8 × 60 ]

Time = 476.28 ÷ 16.632 = 315 / 11 ≈ 28.63 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 28.6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Tank Dimensions: Length (L) = 12 m, Breadth (B) = 9 m, Height (H) = 4.41 m

Pipe Diameter = 21 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 21 / 200 m

Flow Speed (v) = 8 m/s

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a Cuboid = L × B × H

Volume of water discharged per second = Area of cross-section × Flow Speed = πr²v

 
 
 
 v = 8 m/s d = 21 cm 
 
 12 m 4.41 m 9 m Empty Tank Flow 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of the tank = 12 × 9 × 4.41 = 476.28 m³

⇒ Area of pipe cross-section = πr² = (22/7) × (21/200) × (21/200) m²

⇒ Volume of water flowing per second = (22/7) × (441/40000) × 8 m³/s

⇒ Volume of water flowing per minute = [(22 × 63 × 8) / 40000] × 60

⇒ Volume of water flowing per minute = 665280 / 40000 = 16.632 m³/min

⇒ Time taken = Volume of tank ÷ Volume per minute

⇒ Time taken = 476.28 ÷ 16.632 = 315 / 11 minutes

⇒ Time taken = 28.636... minutes

⇒ Rounded to one decimal place, Time = 28.6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 28.6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cylinder & Cuboid

Volume of a cylindrical pipe is evaluated as πr²h, and Volume of a cuboidal tank is evaluated as L × B × H.

Flow Rate Concept

When fluid flows through a pipe, the length of the liquid column passing in a given time equals its speed (v × t). The total volume discharged is A × v × t.

Unit Conversion Standard

Always ensure uniform units before calculation. Here, diameter in cm is converted to meters (21 cm = 0.21 m) to match the tank's dimensions and the fluid's flow speed in m/s.
